items.text: Today, the widely held view of advertising. <break time="0.8s" /> Particularly in relation to established brands. <break time="0.8s" /> Is that its role is not to directly increase sales. <break time="0.8s" /> And that, even when it does have this effect. <break time="0.8s" /> The sales generated are generally insufficient. <break time="0.8s" /> To recover the cost of the campaign. <break time="0.8s" /> What then is the purpose of advertising. <break time="0.8s" /> If not to directly increase sales. <break time="0.8s" /> Amongst todays advertising practitioners. <break time="0.8s" /> It is argued. <break time="0.8s" /> That its value lies in improving the consumers attitude towards brands. <break time="0.8s" /> Thus leading to long term sales. <break time="0.8s" /> In this way. <break time="0.8s" /> The real effect of advertising is not at the point of sale. <break time="0.8s" /> But at the point of consumption. <break time="0.8s" /> Consumer brand opinions are only formed. <break time="0.8s" /> After consumers have tried the brand. <break time="0.8s" /> However, these opinions are clearly influenced. <break time="0.8s" /> By the expectations created by advertising. <break time="0.8s" /> In this way. <break time="0.8s" /> Advertising ― the repetition of arguments, creatively presented ―. <break time="0.8s" /> Does not influence product perception. <break time="0.8s" /> At the time it is seen. <break time="0.8s" /> But it does increase the likelihood. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a consumer making an exploratory purchase of the brand. <break time="0.8s" /> And has a strong influence. <break time="0.8s" /> On how he or she feels about the product. <break time="0.8s" /> Compared to the competition. <break time="0.8s" /> Todays advertising seeks to cultivate consumers attitude. <break time="0.8s" /> By promoting their expectations and trials of the brand. <break time="0.8s" /> To encourage long term consumption.
